summaries.demographer: Chau Wang is a 14-year-old Taiwanese American male living in Holualoa, Hawaii, with both parents, a younger sister, and grandparents in a multigenerational household (Q05, Q11, Q51, Q89). He is U.S.-born in Kailua-Kona, currently enrolled full-time in school, and has completed less than ninth grade (Q86, Q87, Q90-Q92). He has never been married, has no romantic partner or children, and is not in the workforce (Q16, Q19, Q84). His household appears stable and family-owned, with parents handling finances and healthcare while maintaining a budget-conscious lifestyle (Q55, Q58, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Chau shows strong future orientation and disciplined resource allocation for a young teenager, saving small amounts for robotics parts, Arduino components, tournaments, and long-term travel goals (Q61, Q62). His choices are shaped by family norms around education, budgeting, and responsibility, as well as by competitive incentives in robotics and soccer (Q02, Q05, Q83). He is loss-averse about wasting money and time, comparing prices and delaying discretionary spending like bubble tea when larger goals matter (Q60-Q64). His main self-control challenge is time, especially late-night coding that trades off against sleep and athletic performance (Q15, Q32, Q44).
summaries.political_scientist: Chau is too young to vote but expects to vote when eligible and already tracks issues involving schools, ocean protection, infrastructure, fairness, and STEM access (Q23, Q24). He identifies as independent or undecided but closer to the Democratic Party on climate, education, science, and equal treatment (Q95, Q96). His civic orientation is local and community-minded, expressed through student council scheduling, beach cleanups, and concern for public schools and environmental protection (Q17, Q24, Q67). On race and policing, he is attentive and somewhat affected by Black Lives Matter, preferring listening, school discussion, and family conversation over protest or public posting (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Chau presents as conscientious, structured, competitive, and technically curious, with a strong identity around reliability, problem solving, and preparation (Q01, Q02, Q43, Q109). He manages stress through planning, lists, physical activity, ukulele, hiking, coding, and family support, though he can become perfectionistic and sleep-deprived when debugging (Q32, Q43, Q44, Q50). He does not report depression or diagnosed anxiety, but he experiences performance-related anxiety before tests, competitions, and games (Q45). His self-concept integrates Taiwanese American family expectations, Hawaii community rootedness, STEM ambition, athletic discipline, and environmental values (Q01, Q47, Q108, Q109).
